findings.reason: verify.sh:277-279 builds the probe with an unquoted heredoc (`<<SH`). Inside it, `\"` keeps its backslash, so the remote sh runs `command -v \"jq\"`. That looks up the name `"jq"`, quotes included, finds nothing and exits with missing_binary. runtime-binaries.json:4-8 lists jq first with method system, a non-wrapper, so the first loop iteration fails and check 3 calls fail whenever GCE_INSTANCE_NAME is set.
findings.claim: The non-wrapper probe looks up a binary name with literal double quotes in it (`command -v \"jq\"`). So check 3 fails on every GCE Verify run, even when jq is installed, and checks 4 onward never run.
findings.evidence: The probe is built with an unquoted heredoc: `nonwrapper_probe="$(cat <<SH ... binary_path="\$(command -v \"${binary}\" || true)"`. In an unquoted bash heredoc, a backslash escapes only `$`, backtick, `\` and newline, so `\"` stays as `\"`. The generated script therefore reads `binary_path="$(command -v \"jq\" || true)"`. `shell_single_quote` passes that through unchanged to `sudo docker exec <container> sh -c '...'`. Inside the `$(...)`, dash parses `\"jq\"` as the word `"jq"` (with quote characters), so `command -v` finds nothing, `|| true` leaves `binary_path` empty, and the probe exits with `missing_binary:jq`. `jq` is the first entry in scripts/docker/runtime-binaries.json and uses `install.method: system` (not a wrapper), so the first loop iteration hits `|| fail "Failed to validate runtime binary jq in ..."`. The outer call at line 361 then fails. Check 3 runs whenever `GCE_INSTANCE_NAME` is set, which covers both staging and production.

findings.reason: The diff reads the entries with jq from `${repo_root}/scripts/docker/runtime-binaries.json` (diff line 236). The in-image manifest only gets `test -f`. verify.yml:35 checks out with no ref, while deploy-staging-on-release.yml:36 and promote-production.yml:9 verify an image tied to another ref or image_ref. A mismatch can therefore happen, though only when the manifest has drifted between those commits.
findings.claim: The runtime binary check reads its list of binaries from the manifest in the runner's checkout instead of the one baked into the deployed image, so an image built from another commit is checked against the wrong list.
findings.evidence: Line 357 sets `runtime_binary_manifest_in_repo="${repo_root}/scripts/docker/runtime-binaries.json"`, and line 252 runs `jq ... "${runtime_binary_manifest_in_repo}"` on the runner. The manifest inside the image (`/usr/local/share/openclaw/runtime-binaries.json`, installed by Dockerfile:135 and Dockerfile.sandbox:23) only gets `test -f` (lines 240-243); its contents are never read. The removed probe ran `jq` on the in-image manifest, so the image was always checked against its own manifest. .github/workflows/verify.yml:35 uses `actions/checkout@v4` with no `ref`. deploy-staging-on-release.yml calls verify from a `workflow_run` trigger, where the default checkout is the default branch, but the image under test is built from `github.event.workflow_run.head_sha` on daisy/dev. If those branches differ, the two manifests may disagree.

findings.reason: verify_runtime_binaries_for_target calls gce_ssh for the manifest check, the arch check, and once or twice per entry. With about 12 entries that is roughly 15 SSH calls per target, against 1 before. This is a performance point, so it stays low.
findings.claim: The check now opens one IAP SSH session per manifest entry, plus one container per check in image mode, where before it made one call per target.
findings.evidence: Each target runs `gce_ssh` for the manifest check (242) and the arch check (247), once per non-wrapper entry (295), and twice per wrapper entry (267, 271). With the 12 amd64 entries (11 non-wrapper plus gemini), that is about 15 `gcloud compute ssh --tunnel-through-iap` calls for the gateway and 15 more `docker run --rm` sessions for the sandbox image. Before the change, each target made a single `gce_ssh` call.
